speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I had four Budgets, two Ministerial Statements and the Budget Round-ups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, my new year wish is to have one Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members will bear with me that this Budget speech will be very long and I hope that you stay alert over the next two to three hours.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have spent a year fighting the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The pandemic-triggered recession has hit both demand and supply side simultaneously.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We averted the worst, and prevented deep economic scarring and permanent impairment of our economic strengths.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last week, the Ministry of Finance released an interim assessment of the COVID-19 Budget measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our early findings show that the combination of fiscal, monetary, and transitional measures, mounted as a whole-of-Government response, has helped to avoid a worse recession, avert job losses, and mitigate inequality.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Lower-income households received higher levels of support from some of the COVID-19 measures, such as the Workfare Special Payment and Grocery Vouchers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While fiscal measures did most of the heavy lifting, the measures taken by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, to maintain an accommodative monetary policy stance, ease cash flow constraints and ensure sufficient liquidity in the banking system, complemented the fiscal measures well.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of Law’s COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act 2020 also offered temporary relief to individuals and businesses for rental and various other contractual obligations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the public health front, community cases have remained low and we have been on a path of gradual re-opening since June last year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We were able to mount a whole-of-Government response to COVID-19 decisively, without incurring a huge debt for future generations, because successive generations have built up strong reserves ahead of this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we re-opened our economy, we shifted our measures from containment to restructuring, while continuing our support for Singaporeans, workers and businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We transitioned our broad-based support to more targeted ones for firms, especially those in the hardest-hit sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We shifted our focus from job retention to job creation, and helped workers secure jobs in growth sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We set up the Emerging Stronger Taskforce amid the crisis to respond to the new realities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The global battle against COVID-19 is far from over.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many places are still experiencing high levels of infection.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The recovery in global economic activity is expected to be long-drawn, highly uncertain, and uneven across sectors and geographies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The arrival of vaccines gives us hope that economies and borders can re-open more quickly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Vaccinating a large proportion of the population will take some time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The emergence of more infectious variants may raise the threshold for herd immunity and disrupt the resumption of economic activities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If a new strain that is resistant to existing vaccines emerges, a new round of vaccination will be needed, further delaying economic recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This uncertainty is accentuated by several structural trends and challenges, including some brought to the fore by the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, the rising protectionism over supply chains, resources, data and technology.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This has been accelerated by a heightened sense of vulnerability and distrust during the crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, the unprecedented levels of public debt globally to finance the extraordinary fiscal responses during the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These add to concerns over long-term sustainability of debt and risks of inflation over time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The trajectory of the pandemic will determine the immediate trajectory of the global economic recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a small, open economy, Singapore’s economic recovery is contingent on how the global situation plays out.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need to adapt nimbly to the wide range of possible outcomes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since our independence, Singapore has weathered crisis after crisis, and emerged stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am confident that we, as Singaporeans, can once again summon our resolve to tackle the challenges, and emerge stronger from this unprecedented crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us seek to build a stronger Singapore: That is economically vibrant, so we can create good jobs for our people and opportunities for our businesses; That is socially cohesive, with a strong social compact and community spirit; That is a welcoming home, green and sustainable for generations to come; That has the fiscal and social reserves to enable continued stability and progress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Budget 2021 deploys our fiscal resources and the energies of our people, to realise our collective aspirations and build our future together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will now elaborate on our plans, with the details in the Annexes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The global economy is projected to recover to pre-COVID-19 levels this year, but the recovery is uneven across countries and sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Package will have three prongs: first, to address our immediate needs to safeguard public health and re-open safely; second, to support workers and businesses where needed; third, to target support for sectors that are still under stress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The first prong is to safeguard the health of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We started our vaccination programme late last year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I strongly encourage Singaporeans and residents who are medically eligible to take the vaccine when your turn comes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, we must continue to contain the spread of the virus, by keeping up our precautionary measures and our multi-layered defence system of contact tracing, testing and safe distancing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second prong of our Package is to continue support for workers and businesses where needed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 continues to affect many of our workers and businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When COVID-19 first hit, I introduced the Jobs Support Scheme, or JSS, with a clear goal to protect jobs and help firms retain local workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the situation deteriorated in the ensuing months, I enhanced the wage support level and its duration, and brought forward the disbursement timeline.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The current tranche will continue to cover wages up to March 2021 for most sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am heartened that many employers have managed to retain and reskill their workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as our economy recovers gradually and some sectors grow well, some other sectors remain stressed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will tailor support to maintain resilience and support growing areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, I will continue to provide JSS, targeted towards sectors that continue to be hard-hit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms in these sectors will receive 30% support for wages paid from April to June 2021, and 10% support for wages paid from July to September 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For firms in Tier 2 sectors, such as retail, arts and culture, food services and built environment, I will extend JSS at 10% for three months, covering wages paid up to June 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This excludes segments like supermarkets which are classified as Tier 3B.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For firms in Tier 3A sectors, JSS will continue covering wages up to March 2021, as previously announced.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Nightlife establishments such as pubs, and karaoke outlets, are not yet permitted to re-open.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They can apply for grants from the Ministry of Trade and Industry and Enterprise Singapore to pivot to other permissible activities or wind down.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, to facilitate workers moving to jobs in growth areas, I will be extending specific schemes within the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package, including the Jobs Growth Incentive and specific traineeship, attachment and training opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, I extended the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme and the enhanced Enterprise Financing Scheme – Trade Loan till 30 September 2021, to ensure businesses have continued credit access.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also enhanced the Enterprise Financing Scheme to better support loans for local construction projects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These programmes have helped many companies in the past year, with more than 20,000 taking up over $17 billion of working capital and trade loans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope businesses will make full use of these schemes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 Resilience Package also funds the COVID-19 Recovery Grant, which supports workers who lost their jobs or experienced significant income loss.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Grant has been open for applications since 18 January 2021, and more than 5,000 applications have been approved as of 15 February 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The third prong of the COVID-19 Resilience Package is to provide more targeted support for the worst-hit sectors, which continue to be adversely affected in 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will need help to maintain capabilities and eventually recover.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, for our aviation sector, the recovery in global air travel will take some time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As of end-January this year, total passenger movements in Changi were only about 2% of pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To preserve core capabilities and Singapore’s strong position built up over the years, I will provide targeted support and extend cost relief for the aviation sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will cost the Government $870 million this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I expect the aviation sector to use this lull to sustain and upgrade its capabilities, and to prepare for the recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In our land transport sector, taxi and private hire car drivers have been hard hit by the pandemic, and will continue to need support in 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will be supported by the COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund, which we announced previously.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have set aside $133 million for this Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The arts and culture, and sports sectors, connect our communities and weave the fabric of our society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These sectors have been deeply affected by the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will extend the Arts and Culture Resilience Package and Sports Resilience Package in FY2021 to support businesses and self-employed persons in these sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also enhance these packages to support capability development and sector transformation, to encourage the community to deepen skills, go digital and transform business models.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth will announce more details on both packages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have covered the COVID-19 Resilience Package, which addresses our immediate needs – to safeguard public health, provide support for workers and businesses, and give more help to worst-hit sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The past year’s Budgets and the COVID-19 Resilience Package are about preservation and adaptation – to safeguard lives, jobs, supply chains, and core economic capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: From 2021, our focus will be on Emerging Stronger, Together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has triggered global shifts on the economic, social and political fronts, on a scale arguably greater than the 1929 Great Depression.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has set off new domains for competition and cooperation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To secure our future, we must build new capabilities in our people and businesses, and find new ways to work together effectively.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Within and across industries, and beyond our shores.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While the post-COVID-19 global economic landscape is being reshaped and remains uncertain, we can discern the broad contours.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: What are some of the key changes that can affect Singapore?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, the speed of technological advances and re-configuration of global supply chains will reshape competitive advantages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During the 2003 SARS outbreak, by the time vaccines were ready for clinical trials, the virus was already largely contained through public health measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Governments, scientists and industry mobilised to work together at unprecedented speed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 vaccines were developed in less than a year, and tests were implemented within weeks to months, in the US, China, Europe and Russia.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This collaboration across industries and nations, has been a positive side of the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But COVID-19 has also accentuated a US-China-centric technology race, into a global race for technological superiority and heightened concerns over supply chain resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For Singapore, as global supply chains are reconfigured, we must plug ourselves into critical parts of global networks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses will need to transform and digitalise, to plug into the flow of goods and capital.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, COVID-19 has hit countries and communities unevenly and widened inequalities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, this tiny virus has reminded us of the intricate interdependencies of our ecosystem, and the importance of sustainability and biodiversity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our human activities have accelerated changes in our environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must work together to safeguard this fragile eco-system for our future generations, and take climate change seriously.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In short, these three changes – the changing competitive landscape, rising inequalities, and importance of sustainability – are all mega-shifts, that will continue to reshape the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To stay on top of these changes, we must bring all stakeholders together swiftly to respond to and seize the diverse opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, while last year’s Budgets were tilted towards emergency support in a broad-based way, this year’s Budget will focus on accelerating structural adaptations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the face of major changes, we must move from just counter-cyclical fiscal and monetary stabilisation policies, to structural economic policies to equip our businesses and workers with deep and future-ready capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Like many countries, we have devoted significant resources to preserve lives and livelihoods in the face of this pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But what will continue to distinguish Singapore are our investments for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will invest in our people – so they can bounce back and be ready for opportunities that arise; and we will invest in our businesses – so they can innovate, build deep capabilities and seize growth opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore must never stop thinking of the future, even as we respond swiftly to meet current needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is how we stay exceptional, and staying exceptional is how we survive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, to catalyse a wide range of capital to enable businesses to transform and scale.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, to create opportunities and redesign jobs, for our people to develop their skills, creativity and talents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ultimately, the purpose, the raison d'être of our economic transformation is to grow opportunities for our people to realise their full potential and aspirations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a small, open city-state, Singapore has maintained the vibrancy of our society by enabling the global flow of goods, ideas, capital and people through our shores.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 disrupted our physical connectivity but accelerated the rise of the virtual and knowledge economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To emerge stronger, we must deepen Singapore’s position as a Global-Asia node.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will restore our physical connectivity and transform our aviation sector for recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also expand our digital connectivity and deepen our capacity to collaborate and innovate with partners around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Travel and connectivity have taken a severe hit due to COVID-19, and recovery may be prolonged.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, COVID-19 has reshuffled the global web of connectivity, and changed the aviation landscape.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Airports will be differentiated by their capabilities in securing public health and enabling safe travel.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will need digitalised systems and the ability to effectively re-route people and goods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes the Notarise and Verify system being developed by GovTech through private-public partnerships.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, GovTech is working with local start-up Affinidi, on a software that can quickly verify the authenticity of digital COVID-19 test result certificates and vaccination records.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond physical connectivity, the post-COVID-19 economy will see two key shifts: First, a shift from physical to digital modes of transactions across geographical borders.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, a shift from tangible to intangible assets in value creation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Such intangible assets include the knowledge, networks and data that businesses can use to create new technologies and innovations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To remain competitive, businesses will need to innovate and collaborate on a global scale.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support our businesses, I will invest in three key platforms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is especially useful for larger businesses which want to rekindle a start-up mindset within their organisations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One such venture studio which I visited recently is BCG Digital Ventures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They collaborated with Olam, a Singapore food and agricultural multinational to build Jiva, a farmer services platform.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This platform will help farmers in developing countries to increase crop yield, access credit and connect directly to buyers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This venture helps meet the rising global food demand, while uplifting the income of farmers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second platform is the Open Innovation Platform, or OIP.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The OIP facilitates the matching of problems faced by companies and public agencies with solution providers, and co-funds prototyping and deployment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, through the platform, the Building and Construction Authority, was matched with three solution providers, TraceSafe, TagBox and Nervotec, to develop solutions for safe re-opening of worksites.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The firms developed real-time systems that helped construction site owners conduct contact tracing and health monitoring of their workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will enhance the OIP with new features such as a cloud-based Digital Bench for accelerated virtual prototyping and testing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The third platform I will enhance is the Global Innovation Alliance, or GIA.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The GIA serves to catalyse cross-border collaboration between Singapore and major innovation hubs globally.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, despite the pandemic, there were over 100 potential business matches between Indonesian and Singapore-based corporates.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: WaveScan, a Singapore start-up specialising in sensor technology, tapped on GIA and formed a partnership with A.L.I.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Technologies, a company in Japan specialising in unmanned miniature aircraft.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: WaveScan also attracted investments from Leave a Nest, a GIA operating partner in Tokyo.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The GIA will also be enhanced through the inclusion of the Co-Innovation Programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2019, 31 Singapore companies were supported for projects with enterprises from 11 partner countries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One of them, Xnergy, is a local deep-tech start-up with expertise in contactless charging.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through the Co-Innovation Programme, Xnergy partnered with Balyo, a French multinational, to co-develop contactless charging systems for forklifts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As businesses innovate, they will create intellectual property and intangible assets, or IP and IA.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will need to identify and protect, value and manage, and commercialise these.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support businesses in commercialising the fruits of their innovation, we are developing the Singapore Intellectual Property Strategy 2030.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will include equipping businesses with tools to value their IP and IA, and training skilled professionals in these fields.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Intellectual Property Office of Singapore will announce the details on World IP Day in April.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Strong connectivity enables our businesses to plug into global and regional supply chains and industry clusters, and deepen our innovation partnerships.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are stepping this up with ASEAN nations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is significant growth potential in this region, with favourable demographics for the next two decades.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last December, ESG, IMDA and EDB launched the inaugural Southeast Asia Open Innovation Challenge which saw participation from Indonesian, Malaysian, Thai, and Vietnamese corporates.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have also launched cross-border projects through ASEAN platforms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One such project is the YCH Vinh Phuc Inland Container Depot Logistics Centre that was launched last November.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a joint landmark SuperPort project between Singapore-based YCH Group and T&T Group, a Vietnamese conglomerate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To promote the integration of ASEAN markets, we are pursuing common frameworks in emerging areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, ASEAN nations have developed the ASEAN Payment Policy Framework to encourage retail payment linkages between ASEAN countries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to work closely with our ASEAN members, to enhance digital connectivity and cybersecurity, and to get ready for the Fourth Industrial Revolution, building on initiatives such as the ASEAN Smart Cities Network.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also continue to enhance our infrastructure investments in the region.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Kendal Industrial Park was a joint investment between Singapore’s Sembcorp and Indonesia’s PT Jababeka to build up activities in food processing, building materials, and medical equipment manufacturing, amongst other sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In my Statement in October last year, I also announced our intent to enhance cooperation with our most immediate neighbours, through Iskandar Malaysia in Johor, and the islands of Batam, Bintan, and Karimun in the Riau Islands.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One of the goals is to build up a cluster of industries around the electronics, medtech, food manufacturing and processing sectors, as these see rising demand in ASEAN nations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The recently launched Southeast Asia Manufacturing Alliance will support these efforts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It serves to promote a network of industrial parks to manufacturers interested to invest in both Singapore and the region, and connect local firms with these manufacturers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the digital front, we are working with our Indonesian partners to build the Nongsa Digital Park to facilitate collaboration between Singaporean companies and tech talent in Indonesia.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia grow together, benefits will also be reaped by the wider Southeast Asian region.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To summarise, the first enabler is to grow a vibrant business community, with a strong spirit of innovation and enterprise, deeply connected with the ASEAN region, Asia and the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second enabler is to catalyse a wide range of capital to co-fund and enable businesses, from start-ups to small, medium, and large enterprises, to innovate, transform and scale.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses have had to preserve cash flows during these uncertain times.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Yet, it is precisely during these extraordinary times, that those that are ready to seize new opportunities will emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To catalyse the flow of capital and bridge market gaps, the Government will step up risk-sharing arrangements with providers of capital, and provide grants to support businesses at various stages of growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will ensure that they continue to have access to financial capital, by extending and enhancing the Enterprise Financing Scheme - Venture Debt programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: From 2016 to 2019, we have seen an annualised growth rate of 44% in the amount of early-stage funds raised for promising enterprises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our eco-system of budding entrepreneurs and venture funds is growing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, more mature enterprises, from micro and small, to medium and large enterprises, should also invest in new and emerging technologies to sharpen their competitiveness.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To encourage them to do so, the Government will co-fund their adoption of digital solutions and new technologies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The new Emerging Technology Programme will co-fund the costs of trials and adoption of frontier technologies like 5G, artificial intelligence and trust technologies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will support commercialisation of innovations and diffusion of technology downstream.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help firms to identify and adopt digital solutions, a Chief Technology Officer, or CTO-as-a-Service initiative will provide access to professional IT consultancies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A new Digital Leaders Programme will also support promising firms in hiring a core digital team and in developing and implementing digital transformation roadmap.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond these new initiatives, I will also extend the enhanced support levels of up to 80% for existing enterprise schemes such as the Scale-up SG programme, Productivity Solutions Grant, Market Readiness Assistance, and Enterprise Development Grant, to end-March 2022.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the coming years, a critical part of business transformation will be in job redesign.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With technological advances, many tasks that are physically demanding or repetitive can be better done by machines.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With an ageing workforce, we must leverage technology to develop senior-friendly workplaces.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: An example is a household name, Tim Ho Wan.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Working with NTUC’s e2i, it modernised what was previously tedious manual ordering, tabulation and reporting, saving 20-30% in man-hours.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To ensure productivity gains are shared with employees, e2i also negotiated with the company to increase the salary of the impacted older staff.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support the growth of local companies, the Government has partnered equity firms to provide growth capital for companies to transform and scale.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Thus far, we have largely focused our efforts on small and medium enterprises, or SMEs, with annual revenues of up to $100 million.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Companies of this scale traditionally lack attention from private equity players, while larger enterprises tend to have the means to raise capital.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, changes in the global economic landscape and financial markets have made it harder for our large local enterprises, or LLEs to attract private equity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This may mean missed opportunities for companies with strong fundamentals to plug into new areas, as supply chains are reconfigured.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, many have expanded overseas, projecting the Singapore brand as a trusted and reliable partner.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The platform will invest in non-control equity and mezzanine debt of selected LLEs, which are willing to work with the fund manager to pursue their next phases of growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Temasek will bring its strong commercial discipline to this partnership.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry will provide more details on the Fund later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have touched on our support for companies – from high growth to more mature enterprises, from SMEs to LLEs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we can reap the full benefits of transformation, when we transform the entire value chain.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, for the next phase of our industry transformation, I will focus on the transformation of entire value chains – where each player in the chain works together to integrate and digitalise processes, and upskill their workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since the launch of the Construction Industry Transformation Map in 2017, the Government has made a big push to drive transformation in the Built Environment sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms have adopted new ways of doing things, such as Design for Manufacturing and Assembly, or DfMA, and Building Information Modelling.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This sector has just experienced an existential threat last year and is recovering.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Developers, consultants and contractors now realise the urgency to radically improve productivity and reduce the reliance on labour-intensive methods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The GTS for the Built Environment sector will require developers to work closely with their consultants, contractors and suppliers to level up as an eco-system or value chain.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Working together to transform and innovate, the alliance members can achieve more than what each alone can do.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, while we continue support the sector’s recovery, we will tilt our support to enable it to transform decisively.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our resolve in achieving transformation of the industry – and, in fact, of all industries – is clear and unwavering.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for National Development will elaborate on this at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have touched on the first two enablers in our next phase of transformation – to grow a vibrant and connected business sector with a strong spirit of enterprise, and to catalyse a suite of capital tools.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Enabling our people to have access to good jobs and job opportunities is the purpose for developing a strong economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A vibrant economy creates the jobs and opportunities for our people to be at their best.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The employment landscape is undergoing fundamental changes, and COVID-19 will accelerate these changes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A digital, innovation-driven economy means that businesses will need highly-skilled workers and deep talent.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our people will need to have both broader and deeper skills and creativity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has forced us to work from home and adopt new ways of collaborating with others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over 80% of firms intend to implement more flexible working policies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are global trends that our people will have to adapt to. ‘Working from Home’ is just a short step to ‘Working from Anywhere’.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Yes, anywhere in the world – as long as you have a computer and Internet connection.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singaporeans may find more opportunities as the best firms source globally, but will also face stiffer competition from talents who may not even step foot in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are many strengths in Singapore that will enable us to create good jobs here.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But to access these, we have to learn and adapt.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I met Mr Edmund Tang last September, when he was at the e2i Trade and Connectivity Career Fair looking for a job.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He had been working on autonomous vehicles but decided to explore if his skills could be better deployed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: An e2i career coach matched him with a job opening.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, he is a Senior Business Development Manager in the Advanced Remanufacturing and Technology Centre, an A*STAR Research Institute.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In his new role, he is able to build on his experience to develop new skills in a new area and role.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package is a key pillar in our industry transformation, to enable Singaporeans to learn and thrive, as our jobs and workplace change, and as businesses transform.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It was first launched last year, to tackle the anticipated labour market fall-out from COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Looking ahead, as companies and industries transform, and new growth areas emerge, our people will need to have the skills and agility to move.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To emerge stronger, our people will need new knowledge and skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Companies hiring eligible locals will be given up to 12 months of wage support from the month of hire.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, those hiring mature workers, persons with disabilities and ex-offenders will be given up to 18 months of enhanced wage support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For workers who require additional support before landing a job, we will also extend the support for the SGUnited Skills, SGUnited Traineeships and the SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programmes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we head into a more technologically-intensive and innovation-driven economy, we must also groom leaders in innovation and enterprise, especially in deep technology areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The NRF will be supporting about 500 Fellowships under the new Innovation and Enterprise Fellowship Programme, or IFP, over the next five years, to meet needs in areas such as cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and health tech.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will work with a range of partners, including accelerators, venture capital firms and deep tech start-ups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The first partner, SGInnovate, recently launched Power X (Robotics), the first programme under IFP, to develop local talent for the fast-growing robotics and automation sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Trainees undergo a nine-month programme to learn and apply robotics-related skills on real-world projects, and are thereafter placed with their respective host companies to help drive innovation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The inaugural programme has 10 trainees in six host companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One of the trainees, Mr Cheng Yi Chiao, previously worked in various MNCs and start-ups overseas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He returned to Singapore and was emplaced in an agri-tech start-up, Polybee.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Working together with Polybee's team, Mr Cheng has learnt in a very short time how automation of pollination with micro drones works.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These efforts are in line with the enhancement of food security in Singapore with deep tech.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The host companies have welcomed this initiative to build up tech talent in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Next, I will touch on the healthcare sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our healthcare workers have, over the years, been working hard to provide us with the highest quality of care.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since COVID-19 hit, their exemplary commitment has shone through.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Once again, let me express our deepest appreciation to all healthcare workers for your dedication in fighting the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond the pandemic, the healthcare sector is set to grow as our people age.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will apply to workers across public healthcare institutions, and publicly-funded community hospitals and long-term care service providers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Health will announce the details at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some Singaporeans are concerned about our reliance on, and competition from, foreign manpower.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, many businesses and trade associations have said that it is difficult to hire locals, and asked for us not to tighten foreign worker quotas further, to remain globally competitive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The way forward is neither to have few or no foreign workers, nor to have a big inflow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have to accept what this little island can accommodate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To strike a balance, we must focus on enhancing the complementarity of local and foreign manpower, and step up on industry transformation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I urge employers to make use of this and other schemes to redesign jobs and upskill their local staff.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For sectors, especially those in new growth areas, where we may be short of skills, we welcome expatriates with the right expertise to complement Singaporeans and help us build capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will allow us to add vibrancy to the local market, better serve international and regional markets, and enhance Singapore’s attractiveness to global investors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Capability Transfer Programme, or CTP, is one of many programmes that supports such foreign-to-local skills transfer.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One Singaporean who has benefited from the CTP is Mr Mohamad Zaini Bin Selamat.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He is a Technical Officer at SP Services who learnt skills from foreign experts in network support for the roll-out of advanced electricity meters.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He is now performing higher-value work such as fault isolation and data analysis and supervising junior colleagues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To complement our local workforce, we also have the S Pass for companies to hire workers with the technical expertise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I had indicated at the Unity Budget in February 2020, that the Manufacturing S Pass Sub-Dependency Ratio Ceiling, or sub-DRC, would be cut when conditions allow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Manufacturing is a significant pillar of our economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To achieve our vision of being a global advanced manufacturing hub, firms must make it a priority to develop a strong, highly-skilled local core in their workforce.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We cannot do without foreign workers, especially those with deep skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is in line with the tightening already underway in other sectors such as the Services, Construction, and Marine Shipyard and Process sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The move has been carefully calibrated, so that firms have one year to adjust, before changes are implemented.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to review our S Pass framework, including the qualifying salary and levies, to ensure we maintain complementarity between the local and foreign workforces.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have touched on how we plan to emerge stronger as a workforce and as an economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond economic opportunities, what is fundamental is our sense of purpose and our sense of togetherness.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since our independence, we have been seeking to build a fair, just and caring society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have been building strong bonds as a people and deepening our social compact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this pandemic, we have seen how Singaporeans united in adversity and supported one another.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even before COVID-19, many societies were facing sharp divisions due to widening inequalities, increasing diversity of interests and voices, and growing distrust.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The pandemic has deepened the cracks in many societies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to strengthen our social fabric and reject forces of division and discord.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, the Government has been investing significantly in three key areas: We subsidise healthcare heavily to ensure that every Singaporean has access to affordable and quality healthcare.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We invest in education to ensure that every Singaporean has access to opportunities to maximise their potential, regardless of their starting point in life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We promote home ownership, with significant subsidies for public housing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Home ownership enables Singaporeans to share in the nation’s growth, while ensuring a roof over their heads even in times of uncertainty like this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Strengthening our social compact will always be a work-in-progress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we recover from this crisis of a generation, let us strive to emerge stronger as a society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In June last year, we launched the Emerging Stronger Conversations in the midst of the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad that many expressed their wish for a fair, equal and caring society, with more support for vulnerable groups, such as lower-wage workers and persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last June, I also announced that we would form Singapore Together Alliances for Action, or AfAs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These will become a key approach to forging partnerships and cross-sector collaborations to pursue new growth areas, and to tackle complex issues, including those that have come up through the Emerging Stronger Conversations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This AfA will build on the good work of our community partners and individuals, and harness their resources and creativity to co-create solutions to improve support for care-givers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will announce details at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We expect more AfAs to be announced in the months ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the five Budgets last year, we brought immediate relief and support for families and workers, looking out especially for those who were more badly affected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For families, we provided the Care and Support Package and the Solidarity Payment, which benefited all Singaporeans regardless of income or housing type, with more for the less well-off.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For workers, we implemented the COVID-19 Support Grant, the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme and the Temporary Relief Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the vulnerable groups, we disbursed the Workfare Special Payment to lower-income workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Grocery Vouchers and additional GST Voucher – U-Save provided further support for lower-income families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, I will also extend the Service and Conservancy Charges Rebate for all eligible HDB households for another year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be on top of the annual Edusave top-ups for children in Primary and Secondary schools.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singaporeans’ sense of unity and discipline in observing the precautionary measures such as safe distancing and mask wearing has enabled our progress so far in combating the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The discipline and understanding of our local merchants and hawkers have also been important.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, they have been quite affected by the safety measures, especially during the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope that this new tranche of vouchers can bring more business to our hawkers and heartland shops.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To resource this, I will provide an additional grant to the CDCs amounting to $150 million.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More details will be announced by the CDCs later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Altogether, the Household Support Package will cost about $900 million.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Household Support Package provides some support to all families, with lower- to middle-income families receiving more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our President, at the Opening of Parliament, spoke about the strengthening of our social safety nets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To strengthen our social compact, we must work together to address the challenges faced by the more vulnerable members of our society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will continue to allocate resources in our annual Budgets for this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond short-term relief, some Singaporeans have been more badly affected by the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will highlight three groups that need more support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The first group are workers who are earning low wages or facing more challenges with employment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The third group are our children with special needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, we adopt a multi-pronged approach in supporting them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes the enhanced Workfare Income Supplement scheme, Workfare Skills Support scheme, the Progressive Wage Model and Workcare.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In October last year, the Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers was formed to explore ways to uplift the wages and prospects of our lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government’s aspiration is for every sector of the economy to have some form of Progressive Wages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of Manpower will provide details on the approach for expansion later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Next, our older workers may also need more support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government has been exploring ways to enable workers to continue working if they want to.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Prime Minister announced at the National Day Rally in 2019 that we will raise the Retirement Age and Re-employment Age to 63 and 68 respectively in 2022, with the Government and the Labour Movement effecting this a year earlier in 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help businesses adjust, I introduced the Senior Worker Support Package in the Unity Budget last February.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support more companies to move earlier to raise their retirement and re-employment ages, I will increase the budget allocation for the Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant and the Part-Time Re-employment Grant by over $200 million.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of Manpower will provide more details.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Another segment of workers who may face greater challenges in securing or retaining jobs, are persons with disabilities, or PwDs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To encourage employment and training of PwDs, MSF announced two weeks ago, the creation of 1,200 new job and training opportunities for PwDs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This builds on the various initiatives to boost employment for PwDs, such as the Open Door Programme and the Enabling Employment Credit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have touched on the segments of the workers who need more support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second group of Singaporeans who have been badly affected by the pandemic are our lower-income families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MSF has been working to strengthen social service delivery and provide holistic support for our lower-income families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Community Link, or ComLink, is one such initiative.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Introduced in 2019, ComLink has become one of MSF’s key initiatives to help families with children who are staying in rental housing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: ComLink seeks to provide holistic support to low-income families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By mobilising community assets and galvanising local volunteering efforts, ComLink provides families with the tools and support to do better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MSF also ensures that ComLink is coordinated with other initiatives such as UPLIFT and KidSTART, to provide families with seamless, holistic support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since implementation, MSF is supporting about 1,000 families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through this initiative, Mdm Soo’s family is able to benefit from a range of additional support, from grocery vouchers to back-to-school items which help to offset living expenses, to enrichment programmes for her children such as the kidsREAD programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will provide details at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides vulnerable workers and low-income families, the third group we need to pay special attention to is our children with special needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, we have enhanced our support for students with special needs, within MOE schools and in Government-funded special education schools.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Children under seven with developmental needs can benefit from a differentiated approach to help them learn better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Building on these, we will look into piloting an Inclusive Support Programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This pilot integrates the provision of early intervention and early childhood services for children who require up to medium levels of early intervention support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many of these children are already attending pre-schools, and this programme will allow them to be more meaningfully engaged alongside other children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We believe this will benefit all children and help them develop social skills and social inclusion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ensuring equal opportunities for all, and supporting the needy and vulnerable segments of our society are integral to strengthening our social compact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to identify and target groups who may need further support, including emerging groups of workers in more vulnerable areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For self-employed persons, we will continue to study ways to enhance their job security and strengthen their retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government is working with our unions and various agencies on these efforts, including outreach to more self-employed persons.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 crisis has increased a sense of vulnerability among our workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will continue to explore how we can better support our workers to meet the challenges arising from accelerated changes in the economic landscape.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Next, let me talk about how we will emerge stronger as a community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has affected our people in different ways, both tangible and intangible.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While safe distancing measures, especially during our circuit breaker, have enabled us to keep the virus from spreading, they have also caused feelings of loneliness and isolation in some groups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our community partners, charities and Social Service Agencies have stepped up their support well, and the Government will continue to work closely with them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Donations to certain platforms, such as Giving.sg, and for specific causes like COVID-19, have risen.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But donations to many charities in general, and income streams for their recurrent programmes, have fallen.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some charities even had to dip into their reserves to keep operations going.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This affects the help that goes to those who need it.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I encourage individuals and corporates to do more for our charity sector if you can.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have a multi-pronged approach to encourage charitable giving.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes tax incentives for donations made to Institutions of a Public Character or IPCs, and Government grants that match donations raised.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As it stands, the current level of 250% tax deduction on donations to IPCs in Singapore is high, compared to other jurisdictions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, this is set to lapse at the end of 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes donations raised through approved digital platforms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope the additional support will help tide our charities over the crisis, to enable them to do their good work to support the vulnerable in our community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, Community Chest, or ComChest, plays a critical role in raising funds for many Social Service Agencies, including for programmes that uplift lower-income families, such as KidSTART.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The SHARE as One scheme provides dollar-for-dollar matching for new and additional donations through the SHARE programme, which enables corporates, employees and individuals to commit to regular giving.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is potential for businesses to do more to facilitate spontaneous acts of daily giving, for example, by encouraging their customers to make donations at the point of transaction.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will share details at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides philanthropy, we also seek to encourage volunteerism.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses can play an important role in kickstarting their employees’ volunteering journey.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singtel is an example of a strong corporate advocate for employee volunteerism.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: From supporting children and youth with special needs, to enabling digital inclusion for the older generation, Singtel volunteers have been actively engaging the community they serve.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, Singtel employees have been volunteering at Senior Activity Centres to teach seniors how to use smart phones and equip them with basic digital skills to stay in touch with loved ones online and make cashless payments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I encourage our corporates to partner our IPCs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together, we can make a bigger impact to meet the diverse needs of our community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
