text: Despite the stresses that Singaporeans face in this period, we continue to hear many heart-warming stories of our people stepping up to make a difference.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I recently met a group of Singaporeans who came together in the early days of the pandemic to set up N-Lab, a surgical mask manufacturing facility in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They put in close to $1 million of their own capital to design and manufacture masks, and donated many masks to the community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a good example of SG Together – where we come together to make a difference.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is also a testament to the enduring value of NS!

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope these acts of kindness will inspire more people to come forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Apart from national level efforts, efforts by the community – voluntary organisations, corporate partners and individuals – enable us to meet the diverse needs of different groups who need support, especially at the ‘last-mile’.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The tax measures are coming at the end, so I will see whether I can stretch it beyond 5.00 pm!

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will now turn to how we embrace sustainability and build a sustainable home for generations to come.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic reminds us that a pandemic can be an existential threat for humanity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Unlike COVID-19, which was a sudden and sharp shock, climate change is a gradual and intensifying risk, year after year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It can result in extreme weather patterns, which threaten the world’s food and water supply, disrupt global supply chains, diminish biodiversity and upset ecological systems.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Countries, no matter how big or small, must play their part and cooperate with one another.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to support international and regional efforts towards climate action and play an active role at the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change negotiations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our emissions may be just a small fraction of the world’s, but we must do our part.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Sustainable development is a major priority for Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our earlier generations of leaders laid the foundations of long-term planning and sustainable development.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew emphasised the building of a Garden City in our early years and transformed Singapore from a polluted backwater with mucky rivers in 1965, to one of the cleanest and greenest cities in the world today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we have continued to devote resources towards our environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over recent Budgets, the Government has put together plans to tackle climate change and translated them into action.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To improve air quality, we restructured diesel tax in 2017 and 2019.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We introduced a carbon tax, and passed the milestone Resource Sustainability Act in 2019, to encourage enterprises to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions and work towards becoming a zero-waste nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And in 2020, we enhanced our Nationally Determined Contribution, a commitment to further limit our emissions as part of the Paris Agreement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also announced our Long-Term Low-Emissions Development Strategy, which sets out our plans for mitigating and adapting to climate change till 2050 and beyond.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will build on our strong foundations and run a national movement to build a sustainable Singapore for all generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment said in our recent debate on the Motion to Accelerate and Deepen Efforts against Climate Change, sustainability is a journey, not a destination.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our work to achieve sustainable development is never done.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is an ambitious long-term plan that builds on ongoing efforts, to secure a green, liveable and sustainable home for generations of Singaporeans to come.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example: MND is bringing even more greenery to our island home and transforming Singapore into a beautiful City in Nature, while building up carbon sinks by extending nature throughout our island.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MOT is pressing on with our efforts to become a car-lite society by improving public transport, encouraging active mobility, while discouraging pollutive vehicles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MOE is strengthening our education on sustainability practices among our young.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MSE and MTI are leading the push to become more energy- and resource-efficient, develop the green economy and jobs, and invest in urban solutions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a whole-of-society effort to meet a global challenge.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But it is not without constraints and trade-offs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Costs and benefits of projects will change, as climate cost is factored in and as technology advances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to stay open and adaptive, and carefully balance our development objectives with sustainability considerations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Technology is one such game changer and will open new possibilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We harnessed technology to overcome our water and land constraints, and will do the same for climate change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, under the Cities of Tomorrow R&D programme, researchers from A*STAR and HDB led the development of the Integrated Environmental Modeller.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a tool incorporating wind, solar irradiance, shading and environmental noise, to forecast how these factors can affect thermal comfort for residents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has been used by our urban planners in the planning of Tengah Housing Estate, to maximise thermal comfort for residents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Urban Solutions and Sustainability will be a focus area under RIE2025, with investments going towards research to help us build a more sustainable and liveable environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One promising story of innovation by our entrepreneur is the Aquaculture Centre of Excellence, which has innovated and patented “Eco-Ark” with funding support from the Agriculture Productivity Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With advanced aquaculture technologies, Eco-Ark is able to produce 20 times more output than the average in coastal fish farms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This improves our food resilience, as part of the 30-by-30 goal.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment will elaborate at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Technology is also changing the future of transport.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While we are going car-lite, we can further reduce emissions by switching to cleaner-energy vehicles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Electric Vehicles, or EVs, is the most promising clean-energy vehicle technology today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, I announced the expansion of Singapore’s public charging infrastructure for EVs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This enables mass-market electric car buyers to maximise the rebates from the EV Early Adoption Incentive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also revise the road tax treatment for electric cars, by adjusting the road tax bands so that a mass-market electric car will have road tax comparable to an ICE equivalent.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Transport will provide details at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In tandem, we will further discourage the use of internal combustion engine vehicles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore has taken steps to reduce vehicular emissions and we have seen positive outcomes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2017 and 2019, we restructured diesel taxes to shift away from an annual lump-sum tax towards a usage-based tax system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Taxi companies, in particular, have made strides in shifting towards petrol hybrid and electric taxis, with the proportion of diesel taxis in their fleets halving from 86% in 2015, to 42% in 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Usage-based tax has helped shape consumer behaviour towards a more efficient use of fuel, or environmentally-friendly alternatives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To ease the transition for Singaporeans, especially for those who rely on their vehicles for their livelihood, I will provide these support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For motorcycles using petrol, I will provide a 60% road tax rebate to all motorcycles for one year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, individual owners of smaller motorcycles up to 400cc will receive $50 or $80 in cash, depending on engine capacity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For active taxi and Private Hire Car drivers using petrol and petrol-hybrid vehicles, I will provide a Petrol Duty Rebate of $360, given out over four months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is in addition to a one-year road tax rebate of 15% to all taxis and passenger cars using petrol.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For goods vehicles and buses using petrol, I will provide a one-year road tax rebate of 100%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For cars using petrol, I will provide a one-year road tax rebate of 15%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All road tax rebates will take effect from 1 August 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The additional Petrol Duty Rebates for motorcycles, taxis, and Private Hire Cars will be introduced by the middle of 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More details will be released by LTA in April.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Taken together, these measures will offset about one year of petrol duty increases for taxis and motorcycles, and about two-thirds for commercial vehicles and cars.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has also given us an opportunity to change work and travel habits as remote and flexible working arrangements become more common.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A car-lite society will continue to be our main goal.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Public transport is after all the cleanest and most energy-efficient mode of transport.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government has been investing heavily in public transportation and enhancing public transport connectivity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Overall, these measures will work towards reshaping our transport footprint, towards cleaner transport.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The issuance will serve as a reference for the Singapore Dollar corporate green bond market, including the standards and framework applied, and yields achieved.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As an international financial centre, Singapore can catalyse the flow of capital towards sustainable development, not just in Singapore, but in Asia.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MAS has been driving Singapore’s Green Finance Action Plan to develop green finance solutions and markets for a sustainable economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One such green project to be financed with green bonds is Tuas Nexus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Tuas Nexus integrates waste and water treatment facilities, and maximises energy and resource recovery in the solid waste and used water treatment processes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have talked about two key enablers of our Singapore Green Plan – technology and capital.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A third key enabler is the actions of our people – what you and I do, in our daily lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, we have been doing so under the Public Sector Taking the Lead in Environmental Sustainability initiative.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ministries have charted out plans to meet resource targets, such as reducing their electricity and water consumption, and achieving Green Mark standards for our buildings.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some agencies, including the Ministry of National Development, Home Team Academy and Temasek Polytechnic are switching to low-global warming potential refrigerant chillers, ahead of the mandatory adoption in end-2022.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will reduce 24 kilo-tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions, equivalent to the annual emissions of about 7,400 cars.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As part of the Singapore Green Plan 2030, the Government will be committing to more ambitious goals under the “GreenGov.SG” initiative for the public sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This gives renewed focus to the public sector’s contribution towards national sustainability goals, and reminds all public officers that sustainability must be at the core of our work.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment will provide further details on the GreenGov.SG initiatives at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also urge businesses and households to play their part in protecting our environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since then, the effects of climate change have intensified and global momentum to address climate change has accelerated significantly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Countries’ climate ambitions have increased, with the number of countries with net-zero targets increasing from four at end-2017 to 57 at end-2020, including Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On Singapore’s part, we enhanced our 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution and submitted our 2050 Long-Term Low-Emissions Development Strategy under the Paris Agreement in March 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are working towards achieving our long-term net-zero aspirations as soon as viable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This House has also acknowledged that climate change is a global emergency and has called on the Government to take stronger climate actions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, we are in a new situation today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Up until 2023, the carbon tax level will be maintained at $5 per tonne of greenhouse gas emissions as previously announced.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will provide businesses with certainty in the current challenging economic climate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As demand for green products and technologies increase globally, businesses can seize new opportunities for growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One example is Durapower, a battery technology and energy storage solutions company that I visited two weeks ago.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Durapower is working with NTU as one of their global research partners to develop high-energy density lithium-ion battery cells that are lightweight, and have higher power density for fast charging capabilities in EVs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The batteries by Durapower are used in more than 45 cities in over 20 countries across the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is now diversifying into marine and stationary energy storage segments, and further expanding overseas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last but not least, I encourage all Singaporeans to play our part.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad that our youth have been especially passionate about this cause and want to be part of this effort.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the spirit of SG Together, the Government will partner Singaporeans and support ground-up projects which aim to build a more sustainable future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have received more than 200 proposals from individuals, grassroots and businesses for the first SG Eco Fund grant call.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These proposals seek to address a wide range of environmental sustainability challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I welcome all Singaporeans with ideas for sustainable development to step forward and make the difference.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ultimately, building a green Singapore will require a whole-of-society effort, and I hope that we can harness the ideas and energies of the public, private and people sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together, we can build a sustainable home for all.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have laid out the Government’s priorities in the coming years: First, to continue providing relief in the immediate term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, to invest strategically for growth and press on with our economic transformation in the medium term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Lastly, to lay the groundwork to position Singapore for the long term, and build a caring and sustainable home for all.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our fiscal approach must strike a careful balance between addressing our immediate needs and meeting our longer-term structural needs in a responsible manner.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the immediate term, running a fiscal deficit to support targeted relief is warranted, considering the unprecedented impact of COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the longer term, COVID-19 has not changed the fundamental drivers of our fiscal trends.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With our ageing population and maturing society, our recurrent needs in areas like healthcare and other social spending will continue to rise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must meet these structural needs in a disciplined and sustainable way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Hence, beyond this crisis, we must return to running balanced Budgets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It was fiscal prudence and discipline that allowed us to accumulate our national reserves, which has enabled us to respond decisively to this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the last Financial Year, FY2020, we were expecting to draw up to $52 billion from Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the effective response of our people and businesses in adapting to the changing situation, we have been able to bring the pandemic largely under control.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Hence, our requirements for some areas such as public health turned out to be lower than what was provided for.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This means that $9.3 billion is not expected to be used in FY2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This package is needed to safeguard public health, and support our people and businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Given the extraordinary and temporary nature of these measures, the Government proposes to fund the COVID-19 Resilience Package through a draw on our Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a net increase of $1.7 billion from what we expected to draw from Past Reserves to respond to the crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The President has given her in-principle support for the proposed draw of up to $11 billion on Past Reserves in FY2021, to continue the provision of public healthcare and relief measures in the coming Financial Year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Once again, I thank the President for her support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the second consecutive Financial Year where we will be drawing on our Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is necessary, given the exceptional circumstances we are in.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are extremely fortunate to be able to tap on our strategic assets and deploy the resources required to deal decisively with COVID-19 and the considerable uncertainties that lie ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We should never take our reserves for granted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the coming years, our fiscal situation is expected to be tighter.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Fellow Singaporeans have often expressed the desire to better care for our seniors, with quality yet affordable health and aged care services.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is possible only if we can muster the resources to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As our needs grow, we must plan for the resources to fund these, and target the spending in a fair and effective way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has also raised economic uncertainties for citizens and workers, which calls for stronger social safety nets to protect those who are disadvantaged or more vulnerable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will mean higher recurrent spending going forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have maintained the principle that recurrent expenditure should be funded by recurrent revenue.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This ensures that we spend in a responsible way – one that is fair for current and future generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To finance our recurrent spending needs, I first announced in Budget 2018 that we would need to raise the GST rate sometime from 2021 to 2025.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As announced in the Unity Budget in February 2020, in view of economic conditions then, the GST rate increase would not take effect in 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Without the GST rate increase, we will not be able to meet our rising recurrent needs, in particular healthcare spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While we are fortunate to be able to tap on our reserves to respond to the COVID-19 crisis, it is not tenable for the Government to run persistent Budget deficits outside periods of crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: No Finance Minister likes to talk about tax increases, certainly not when the pandemic is still raging around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we do this because we plan for the long term and do not shy away from explaining to fellow citizens why we need to make tough but necessary decisions to ensure that we have enough to provide for our nation’s future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For lower-income Singaporeans, the offset will be even higher, with those living in one- to three-room HDB flats receiving about 10 years’ worth of additional GST expenses incurred.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over and above the transitional support, we already have the permanent GST Voucher scheme to defray GST expenses for lower- and middle-income households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a permanent feature of our system and will be enhanced when the GST rate increase takes place.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through this scheme, we are able to provide targeted support to those who need help most.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Based on past collections, foreigners residing in Singapore, tourists and the top 20% of resident households are estimated to account for over 60% of the net GST borne by households and individuals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is after taking into account the GST Voucher scheme and GST refunded under the Tourist Refund Scheme for goods bought locally for consumption abroad.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If you consider our entire system of taxes and benefits, it is a progressive one.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2020, the top 20% of Singaporean households paid 56% of the taxes and received 11% of the benefits; whereas the bottom 20% paid 9% of the taxes and received 27% of the benefits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, our tax system must remain resilient to withstand shocks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are mindful of international tax developments and the downside risks to our revenues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are on-going discussions to revise international tax rules under the Base Erosion and Profit Shifting, or BEPS 2.0 project.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These proposals will adversely impact our corporate income tax revenues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As I have mentioned in this House previously, we are actively involved in these talks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If and when international tax rules are changed, we will consider if adjustments are required to our corporate tax system accordingly, in consultation with the industry.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One aspect of a fair and resilient tax system is ensuring a level playing field for our local businesses vis-à-vis their overseas counterparts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is especially relevant as e-commerce for sales of goods and services, is growing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In Budget 2018, I announced the extension of GST to imported services from 1 January 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also shared that we would be reviewing international developments on how GST can apply on imported goods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, low-value goods imported via air or post are not subject to GST, to facilitate clearance at the border.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In contrast, GST is paid on such goods purchased in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This change, together with the change announced in Budget 2018, will ensure a level playing field for our local businesses to compete effectively.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Overseas suppliers of goods and services will be subject to the same GST treatment as local suppliers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: IRAS will continue to work with the industry to ensure smooth implementation for the change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also make some tax adjustments to support businesses, and to maintain the competitiveness and resilience of our tax system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The details of these tax changes are in the Annex.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition to meeting our recurrent spending needs, we have also been making significant investments to build Singapore and transform our economy, even before COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I had shared in previous Budgets that the Government is exploring the use of borrowing to finance major, long-term infrastructure that benefit current and future generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This approach will allow us to spread out the lumpy costs of such infrastructure investments more equitably across generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These new bonds allow for a fair and efficient way of distributing the fiscal responsibility.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Fair, because these payments are borne by the generations who will directly benefit from the improved infrastructure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Efficient, because they allow us to benefit from the current low interest rate environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Prior to this, the Government has been issuing bonds to develop the domestic debt market and meet the investment needs of the CPF for Singaporeans’ retirement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will use SINGA borrowing proceeds in a prudent and transparent manner.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These proceeds will be used to finance assets that are crucial to Singapore’s long-term development and sustainability.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These include new MRT lines and infrastructure to protect ourselves against rising sea levels.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is based on the expected pipeline of major, long-term infrastructure projects over the next 15 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also include other safeguards in legislation, which will be open to Parliamentary and public scrutiny.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have briefed the President and obtained her in-principle support for the use of Government borrowing to finance major, long-term infrastructure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More details will be provided when the Bill is presented in Parliament later this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have spoken about our approach for the immediate COVID-19 Resilience Package, and our differentiated approach to address recurrent needs through recurrent revenues and borrowing to finance major, long-term infrastructure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: How we recover from COVID-19 in the next few years is critical.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond dealing with its immediate impact, we are making significant investments to position Singapore for our next bound of growth in the post-COVID-19 world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has disrupted business models and global supply chains, and accelerated trends such as digitalisation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To secure our future, it is crucial for us to seize opportunities in new growth engines, respond to structural trends and transform our economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will invest strategically in these areas over the next few years, so as to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have announced some of these measures in this Budget, while others are being developed by the Emerging Stronger Taskforce, the various Alliances for Action and our agencies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Based on the current outlook, we expect that as the economy recovers, we will be able to balance our Budgets, and our revenues will be able to support projected expenditure for these measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This assessment assumes that the global COVID-19 situation comes under control by next year, enabling economic recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, if the global public health and economic outlook worsen, we may not be able to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have carefully thought through the different scenarios.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While we expect economic recovery in Singapore and globally, there is a wide cone of uncertainty.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even if the economic and fiscal situation turns out to be worse than expected, we must still press on to invest in new areas, so as to ride on the structural changes, transform and emerge stronger as an economy, and as a people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have briefed the President on the Government’s strategy and contingency plan, in the event of a prolonged impact of the pandemic on the economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The President has expressed her understanding towards the Government’s approach, and will consider the Government’s specific proposals, should there be a need to draw on Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the largest Budget deficit since our nation’s independence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The deficit is driven by lower revenues due to dampened economic activity and the significant expenditures needed to mount a decisive response to COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For FY2021, our Budget position remains expansionary as we continue to tide Singaporeans and our businesses over this crisis with the COVID-19 Resilience Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In Mandarin):    Last year, the Government committed nearly $100 billion for relief measures to deal with the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This has helped mitigate the impact caused by the economic recession and played a critical role in protecting our health, our businesses and our livelihood.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Although the vaccine has been developed, various parts of the world are still facing the impact of the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The road to recovery is bumpy and full of uncertainties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, it will be used to protect the health of our people, and support the vaccination programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I urge everybody to take the vaccine to protect yourself and the people around you.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To assist businesses which are still under stress, the Government will once again extend the Job Support Scheme (JSS).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For sectors which are most adversely affected, that is, aviation, aerospace and tourism, the JSS will be extended for another six months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Other sectors, such as retail, arts and culture, F&B and built environment, the extension will be for another three months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The sectors which are hit badly, such as aviation, land transport, arts and culture, and sports will receive additional assistance to help them maintain their core capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will strengthen the connectivity between Singapore and Asia, as well as the whole world, to promote the flow of goods, talents, data and so on.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To do so, the Government will provide various platforms to encourage more businesses to seek co-operation with other companies, and venture into the regional markets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will also launch and extend our suite of capital tools and grant schemes to assist businesses in financing and help them transform and expand their operation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In order to encourage our people to upgrade their skills, and help businesses to re-design their jobs, the Government will extend programmes, such as the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package and the Capability Transfer Programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the other hand, we will also raise the salaries of our nurses and some other healthcare workers, and attract more to join this meaningful field.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes a one-off GST Voucher - Cash Special Payment and the CDC Vouchers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the next two years, the Government will also expand ComLink nationwide.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will benefit more families living in rental flats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, I hope that everybody will uphold the SG Together spirit, and I encourage more people to give back to society and support the charity sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We want to ensure the sustainable development of Singapore and build a green home for generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will work together with the people to advance the Singapore Green Plan to deal with climate change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also accelerate the development of electric vehicle charging infrastructure to better support the growth of electric vehicles and to reduce carbon emission.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All in all, our fiscal space will be further tightened.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must balance between our short-term and our long-term needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I mentioned last year that I will not raise the GST rate in 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As for the specific timing, we will decide based on our economic outlook.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This approach will allow us to spread out the lumpy costs of such infrastructure investments more equitably across generations, avoid substantial increase in taxes, as well as embody the values of collective responsibility.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our past reserves are the “blood-and-sweat” money accumulated by generations of people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Therefore, we must cherish it and put it to good use, carefully.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the past one year, our people cared for one another and fought against the pandemic together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our forefathers managed the nation’s finances prudently, and saved up for rainy days in the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These values (of prudence and care for our future) keep us united and resilient in face of adversity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To sustain this spirit, we need to keep up the mutual trust between our people and the Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For Singapore to continue to be successful, we also need to forge trust with people around the world and collectively look for solutions to our future challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us put our hearts together and emerge stronger to build an even better future for our children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, we will make Singapore into a shining, red dot that commands the trust of all the countries in the world on the global stage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In English): Speaker, Sir, I will now conclude in English.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The first thing I must say is a heartfelt thank you.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And also, to our Labour Movement and tripartite partners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also thank the many Singaporeans who participated in our various consultation sessions, and officers in our Ministries and agencies who have contributed in the design of our schemes, and in ensuring that our programmes reach out to our people, workers and businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A special note of thanks to my very dedicated team of officers in the Ministry of Finance, and my personal assistants, who have been working non-stop since COVID-19 hit the world last year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They continued to work over Chinese New Year and Valentine’s Day – so you see, this is a labour of love.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also thank the Nanyang Polytechnic students who did the illustrations in the slides accompanying my speech.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, I extend the same admiration and thanks to all our frontline, healthcare and essential workers, who have been heroic in keeping our country running and keeping us safe through this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Most of all, Mr Speaker, I wish to thank our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For showing understanding, strength and care, and standing together as one.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I speak on behalf of all of us who have worked hard on this and previous Budgets when I say: Your well-being has been our purpose, and your spirit has been our inspiration.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this Budget, I have outlined our plans to continue to tackle our immediate challenges and to emerge stronger in the new normal.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are no textbook or model answers to deal with such a sudden, unprecedented shock.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Instead, as the situation turns swiftly, we have to assess, adapt and innovate, to tackle the crisis on all three fronts – safeguard lives, jobs and businesses, and our future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our people rallied together, to support one another.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Everyone has been doing his or her part, to observe precautions, however inconvenient, to keep each other safe.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses have been doing their best to adapt and retain workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our healthcare and frontline officers have displayed great courage and dedication.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many charities and volunteers have stepped up their support for those with needs, despite many difficulties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The past year showed that our values as a people matter – the values of unity, resilience, solidarity and fortitude.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The values of care and partnership, of adaptability and action, of working together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our whole-of-society response is greater than the sum of its parts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This sense of togetherness in turn rests on trust – trust in each other, in institutions and in our leaders.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This trust is not just among Singaporeans, but with people around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A very successful overseas entrepreneur saw me recently.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He saw Singapore as a key base to operate and grow, especially in a sustained global pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He saw how we had worked together in Singapore, and with people around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are a safe, trustworthy node and we look ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us continue to focus on what lies ahead and chart a clear direction forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us continue to think long-term, tackle long-term challenges such as climate change and future pandemics, and forge partnerships with people around us, in Singapore, as part of Singapore Together, and with people around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us strive to emerge stronger together, as a united and shining red dot, trusted by all!
